name: Crispy Mongolian beef mince with rice noodles, Tenderstem & edamame

source.author: Pasted recipe text (English)
source.notes: Crisp-seared 5% lean beef mince tossed with rice noodles, Tenderstem broccoli and edamame in a reduced-salt soy / hoisin / honey / rice-vinegar sauce, finished with lime and sesame. Serves 2 generously. The post states 53 g protein and 12 g fibre per serving; the independent estimate here agrees on protein (~53 g) and lands a little lower on fibre (~10.7 g). Already uses reduced-salt soy and lean mince, so it starts well-optimized. Estimate.

serving_desc: ≈575 g cooked (batch ÷2) — a large, complete one-bowl meal

ingredients.item: spring onions, whites and greens separated

steps: Cook the rice noodles until just tender; drain, rinse briefly in cold water and drain well.
Simmer the broccoli and edamame 3–4 min until bright and just tender; drain well.
Whisk the two soy sauces, hoisin, honey, rice vinegar and sesame oil into a smooth sauce.
Sear the beef pressed flat in a hot oiled pan, untouched ~2 min, then break up and crisp 1–2 min more.
Lower to medium, add spring-onion whites, garlic, ginger, chilli and pepper for ~30 sec, then the sauce; bubble 60–90 sec until glossy.
Toss in noodles, broccoli and edamame 1–2 min, loosening with a little hot water if needed. Finish with lime, sesame, spring-onion greens and chilli.

batch_totals.note: Whole dish (2 large servings). Edamame + Tenderstem make this unusually high in fibre and folate for a noodle dish; lean beef brings zinc, iron and B12. Sodium is moderate for a soy/hoisin stir-fry because reduced-salt soy is already used.

him.verdict: A genuinely strong, complete meal: ~53 g protein and ~10.7 g fibre per bowl, with lean 5% beef bringing a big zinc + iron + B12 hit (zinc is one of your sperm-priority micros) and Tenderstem adding a lot of vitamin C. The catch is size — ~686 kcal per serving is a big portion for a cut, and protein density (~7.7 g/100 kcal) is good rather than elite because of the noodles. Split the batch 3 ways, or cut the noodles to ~70 g, and it's a 9.
flags: ~53 g protein + ~10.7 g fibre per bowl
strong zinc, iron, B12 (lean beef) + vitamin C (Tenderstem)
moderate sodium (~1,095 mg) — already uses reduced-salt soy
suggested_mods: Split into 3 portions (~457 kcal / ~35 g protein each) or cut the rice noodles to ~70 g
Swap rice noodles for whole-grain/buckwheat noodles for even more fibre
Drop the honey — hoisin already sweetens the sauce

her_preconception.verdict: Excellent for her: edamame + Tenderstem make it a big folate source, lean beef gives highly absorbable heme iron and B12, and the broccoli's vitamin C boosts iron absorption — all in one bowl. Fully cooked mince, no safety flags.
prenatal_highlights: heme iron + B12 + zinc (lean beef), with vitamin C for absorption

safety_advisories.note: Cook the mince fully through (no pink) — standard for ground beef.

suggested_mods: No changes needed — one of the better prenatal dishes in the library

cooking_guide: Rinse the cooked noodles in cold water and drain very well — it stops them cooking and keeps them springy instead of gluey when tossed later.
Drain the broccoli and edamame thoroughly too; water left on them dilutes the sauce.
For crispy mince, use a genuinely hot pan, press the beef into one thin layer and DON'T touch it for 2 minutes — that undisturbed contact is what builds the browned crust.
Lower the heat before the garlic and ginger go in — they burn in seconds on high heat.
Let the sauce bubble just until glossy but still loose; it thickens further once the noodles go in.
Add hot water a spoon at a time only if it gets sticky. Finish with lime off the heat — the acidity cuts the richness.
